title: Nordic frequency control 2025
description: Nordic synchronous-area frequency control: FCR-N, FCR-D, aFRR and mFRR with synchronous-area volumes, NC ER LFDD from 48.8 Hz to 48.0 Hz, and NC RfG generator frequency protection.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485 (SO GL), Annex III
sources.note: A 0.1 s sub-step and a 120 s catch-up limit are Leitbild modelling choices; they resolve the 0.24 Hz/s RoCoF of the reference incident and the FCR-D activation lag. SO GL Annex III (Nordic: time to restore frequency 15 min, standard range ±100 mHz) frames the time scales.

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Table 7 of the FCR requirements models load frequency dependence Kf = 0.01 p.u./Hz (1 %/Hz) with Sn 42,000 MW / 190,000 MWs and 23,000 MW / 120,000 MWs.

sources.title: Nordic TSOs: Requirements for minimum inertia in the Nordic power system (August 2025)
sources.note: Nordic kinetic energy 2020-24: minimum 110-138 GWs, average 190-195 GWs; design levels 150 GWs (FCR-D performance) and 120 GWs (stability).

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Table 1: FCR-N linear from 0 % at 50.0 Hz to 100 % at 49.9/50.1 Hz; no deadband is allowed and the response must not be artificially delayed.

sources.title: Fingrid: Frequency Containment Reserves (FCR) products
sources.note: Indicative FCR-N response about 63 % within 1 minute and 95 % within 3 minutes, i.e. a 60 s first-order lag. The new requirements specify FCR-N dynamics in the frequency domain instead (disturbance profile 1/(70s+1)).

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Table 1: FCR-D up 49.9 to 49.5 Hz, down 50.1 to 50.5 Hz. Requirement 2: at least 0.86 of steady-state response 7.5 s after the start of a 0.24 Hz/s ramp from 49.9 Hz to 49.0 Hz; the slowest compliant first-order lag is 3.37 s, so 3.3 s is used (derived).

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/631 (NC RfG), Article 13
sources.note: Article 13(1)(a) Table 2, Nordic: 47.5-48.5 Hz 30 min; 48.5-49.0 Hz TSO-specified, at least 30 min; 49.0-51.0 Hz unlimited; 51.0-51.5 Hz 30 min. Generators may disconnect outside these ranges.

sources.title: Statnett: Nasjonal veileder for funksjonskrav i kraftsystemet (NVF 2025)
sources.note: NVF 2025 Table 12-4 (Norway): 47.5-49.0 Hz 30 min; 51.0-52.5 Hz 30 min; synchronous units withstand ±1.5 Hz/s over 1 s.

sources.title: Fingrid: Grid Code Specifications for Power Generating Facilities VJV2024 (unofficial translation 15.1.2025)
sources.note: VJV2024 §10.2.3: withstand 2.0 Hz/s; RoCoF protection may trip only above 4 Hz/s lasting at least 250 ms.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/631 (NC RfG), Article 13
sources.note: The 0.5 s delay of the 47.5 Hz and 51.5 Hz instantaneous elements is a modelling choice; the codes set withstand ranges, not relay delays.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2196 (NC ER), Annex and Article 15
sources.note: Annex, Nordic: start 48.7-48.8 Hz with 5 % of load, final 48.0 Hz with 30 % cumulative, at least 2 steps, at most 15 % per step. Article 15(7)(a): no intentional time delay beyond relay and breaker operating time.

sources.title: Nordic SOA Annex Emergency and Restoration, revised 11/12/2024
sources.note: Nordic LFDD design: five steps at 48.8 / 48.6 / 48.4 / 48.2 / 48.0 Hz, the first four aiming at 5 % each. The 10 % at 48.0 Hz is derived so that the cumulative disconnection reaches the NC ER 30 %.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/1388 (Demand Connection Code), Article 19
sources.note: Article 19(1)(c): LFDD relays operate within 150 ms; used as the stage delay.

sources.title: Nordic SOA Appendix 1 to Annex LFCR: regularly changing parameters 2026
sources.note: Table 5: FCR-N at least 600 MW for the Nordic synchronous area.

sources.title: Svenska kraftnät: How is the FCR volume requirement determined?
sources.note: FCR-D up must cover the reference incident, currently 1,450 MW (Oskarshamn 3).

sources.title: Svenska kraftnät: increased FCR-D down procurement in 2025 (9 December 2024)
sources.note: FCR-D down 1,400 MW, covering full export on NordLink or North Sea Link.

sources.title: Statnett: Technical product and interface specification for delivery of aFRR to Statnett, v4.0 (June 2023)
sources.note: Table 1: aFRR full activation 300 s maximum (120 s preferred); set-points sent no more often than every 4 s, used as the controller cycle.

sources.title: Nordic SOA Annex Load-Frequency Control & Reserves (LFCR), Version 6 (07/02/2024)
sources.note: §7.4.2.2: dimensioned aFRR capacity at least 300 MW (in force through 2025). Version 8 (2026) replaces the figure with a joint Nordic decision; the 2026 Appendix 1 gives at least 200 MW.

sources.title: Statnett: Technical product and interface specification for delivery of aFRR to Statnett, v4.0 (June 2023)
sources.note: Integral time 60 s, no proportional term and a frequency bias equal to FCR-N strength plus load damping are Leitbild tuning; Nordic LFC gains are not published.

sources.title: Fingrid: Terms and conditions for providers of manual frequency restoration reserve (30.9.2026)
sources.note: §7.3.1: mFRR full activation time 12.5 min (2.5 min preparation and 10 min ramp); minimum bid 1 MW.

sources.title: Statnett: confirmation of mFRR EAM go-live 4 March 2025
sources.note: Nordic mFRR energy activation market (EAM) went live on 4 March 2025.

sources.title: Nordic FRR dimensioning methodology under SO GL Article 157 (2022)
sources.note: mFRR volumes of 1,450 MW up and 1,400 MW down mirror the reference incidents; the exact Nordic mFRR dimensioning figures were not verified. The 50 % utilisation threshold held for 120 s that triggers activation is a modelling choice.

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Storage follows the FCR-D up and down bands of Table 1. Its 1 s time constant and 5-95 % state-of-charge window are modelling choices within the requirement.
